title: Vancouver, WA Home Energy Rebates 2026: Clark Public Utilities Water Heater and Heat Pump
desc: Vancouver, Washington home energy rebates for 2026: Clark Public Utilities pays $1,500 for a heat pump water heater, up to $1,250 for a heat pump, $900 ductless and $140 for a thermostat.
h1: Home Energy Rebates in Vancouver, Washington
badge: $1,500 water heater, up to $1,250 heat pump
lead: Vancouver, Washington homes get their rebates from Clark Public Utilities, the public utility for Clark County. About 68 percent of Vancouver homes heat with electricity, so most households can use the utility's offers.
cards_heading: Vancouver home energy rebates at a glance
cards_intro: We read Clark Public Utilities' rebate pages, the State Department of Commerce page and the state solar tax law on October 6, 2026. This page is about Vancouver in Washington State, not Vancouver in British Columbia. Clark Public Utilities rebates are mostly for electrically heated homes.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: For a Tier 3 or Tier 4 unit replacing an electric storage water heater.

cards.title: Central heat pump
cards.note: Depends on whether you replace an electric furnace, a heat pump or zonal heat, and whether the unit is variable-speed. Ductless heat pumps earn $900.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: $0.75 for attics and floors, $1.20 for walls. Duct sealing pays $200 or $500.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: By window rating and the old frame type. Insulated doors earn $40.

cards.title: Smart thermostat
cards.note: Instant rebate at the utility's online marketplace for homes with an electric furnace or heat pump.

cards.title: Solar
cards.note: Clark lists net metering credits and technical help. Washington exempts solar equipment and installation from sales tax through 2029.

after_cards:
Lower-income help

The state gave the City of Vancouver $500,000 for home electrification rebates for households at or below 150 percent of area median income. The state page lists no amount per household. Clark Public Utilities also has income-qualified versions of some weatherization rebates. The federal clean energy credits ended after 2025.
sections:
The US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts 85,421 homes in Vancouver, Washington. About 51 percent of households own and 49 percent rent. About 51 percent of homes are detached houses and about 10 percent sit in buildings of two to four units. This is a newer city than most on our list. About 40 percent of homes were built before 1980, only about 5 percent before 1940, and about 27 percent in 2000 or later.

For main heating fuel, about 68 percent of homes use electricity, 29 percent use utility gas and under 1 percent use oil. That heavy use of electric heat is why Clark Public Utilities' heat pump and weatherization rebates, which are made for electric homes, can reach so many households.

Because fewer Vancouver homes are very old, insulation rebates may apply to fewer of them. Clark's attic rebate needs a starting level of R-19 or less, its floor rebate needs R-11 or less and its wall rebate needs no insulation at all. A home built after 2000 will often be above those levels. Start with the heat pump, water heater and thermostat rebates if your home is newer. Our Clark Public Utilities guide has every amount.
Oregon stores and a Washington rebate

Because Vancouver sits across the Columbia River from Oregon, some shoppers buy water heaters at Oregon stores. Clark's page says a heat pump water heater bought at a participating Oregon Lowe's or Home Depot gets a store markdown through a partnership with the Energy Trust of Oregon and is not eligible for Clark's standard $1,500 rebate. Compare the final price both ways before you buy.
claim_heading: Where to start in Vancouver, Washington
claim_steps: Confirm that Clark Public Utilities sends your electric bill and note what heats your home.
Call an energy counselor at 360-992-3355 with your project.
Start with the $1,500 water heater rebate if you have an electric tank.
Hire a contractor in the utility's Contractor Network for a heat pump.
If your income is at or below 150 percent of area median income, call the City of Vancouver about state-funded rebates.
faq: What rebates does Clark Public Utilities offer?

On our October 6, 2026 reading: $1,500 for a heat pump water heater, $500 to $1,250 for a central heat pump, $900 for a ductless heat pump, $140 for a smart thermostat and per-square-foot weatherization rebates.
Is this about Vancouver, British Columbia?
No. This page is for Vancouver, Washington. For British Columbia, see our BC pages.
Does Clark have a solar rebate?
We did not read a rebate amount. Washington exempts solar equipment and installation from sales tax through 2029 for systems up to 100 kilowatts.
Are the rebates only for electric heat?
Most are. The utility says its weatherization rebates are for electrically heated homes.
Is there a federal tax credit?
No. The IRS says it ended for 2026 installs.
